premise: Ron Calder is a private detective whose gift is imagination: where others see only what happened, he sees what could have happened, and he is often right about the shape of a crime before there is proof. His two closest friends keep him honest: Maya Brandt, a sergeant in the city police, and Arjun Sethi, a lawyer. His dog, Moss, goes everywhere with him, always quiet, always close, never in the way.
spine: Every case runs as an arc of about five episodes, in the same rhythm: a striking opening, Ron's leaps of deduction, a gap he does not see, and an ordinary person doing an ordinary job who mentions a plain fact that makes the truth click. Ron is right about the shape of things and wrong about a detail, and no case is solved by him alone. Arc 1 is an unusual crime that shows how Ron thinks. Arc 2 is Ron's own background, told through a case that reaches into his past. Arc 3 is built around one small object that the story will remember and return to. Later arcs are five episodes each, never fewer than three and never more than seven.
